hero.name: Hoshen Lichi
hero.title: Junior Product Manager Candidate
hero.positioning: I turn real problems into working solutions. With a background in military operations and hands-on AI implementation, I bring structured thinking, user empathy, and a bias for execution to every product challenge.
hero.profileAlt: Hoshen Lichi, Junior Product Manager Candidate
about.p1: Before I knew what product management was, I was already doing it. During my military service, I owned end-to-end solutions: defining requirements, coordinating across teams, and delivering data-driven tools used by 50+ stakeholders. One project I built reduced a manual workload from 12 hours to 2 minutes per week. That experience taught me what it means to own an outcome, not just contribute to one.
about.p2: After my service, I completed the KERNELiOS AI Practitioner program, where I moved through the full product cycle on real problems: identifying user pain points, designing workflows, building AI-powered prototypes, and measuring impact. Every project started with a question: who needs this and why? And ended with something I could put in front of a real user.
about.p3: I'm now focused on junior PM roles where I can bring that same combination of structured thinking, user empathy, and execution bias to a product team.

featured.uiAlt: pick-IT application login screen - agricultural experiment management system
featured.background.heading: Background
featured.background.body: During the KERNELiOS AI Practitioner program, I identified a critical bottleneck in agricultural R&D workflows. Researchers and technicians were managing experiment data through fragmented, inconsistent processes, creating downstream reliability problems across the entire research operation.
featured.problem.heading: User Problem
featured.problem.body: R&D researchers were spending time on manual classification tasks that produced inconsistent results across technicians. There was no unified experiment lifecycle system, resulting in data gaps, missed handoffs, and unreliable outputs. People doing the work had no visibility into the full experiment flow.
featured.goal.heading: Goal
featured.goal.body: Design and deliver an AI-powered experiment management system that standardizes data collection, automates classification, and gives researchers and leads full visibility into experiment status from initiation to close.
featured.constraints.heading: Constraints
featured.constraints.items: No dedicated infrastructure budget; tools had to be accessible|Users had varying technical literacy|System needed to integrate into existing daily workflows, not replace them|Solo product ownership with limited build time
featured.solution.heading: Solution Concept
featured.solution.body: Map the existing experiment lifecycle step by step. Identify where inconsistency and manual effort created the most downstream damage. Replace those touchpoints with structured data collection and AI-assisted classification while keeping the UX familiar to non-technical users.
featured.flow.heading: Main User Flow
featured.flow.items: Researcher initiates experiment via structured intake form|System assigns classification parameters and creates experiment record|Technicians update progress through guided data entry screens|AI layer validates and classifies incoming data in real time|Leads access live experiment status dashboard|On completion, system auto-generates summary report for review
featured.decisions.heading: Key Product Decisions
featured.decisions.items: Scoped AI classification to the highest-friction touchpoint first, not the whole workflow|Chose structured forms over free-text input to improve data consistency at source|Built status visibility into the dashboard as a primary feature, not an afterthought|Produced a stakeholder promo video to drive buy-in before full adoption
featured.metrics.heading: Success Metrics
featured.metrics.items: 20% increase in experiment throughput post-launch|Improved data reliability with fewer classification errors|Adopted by real researchers and technicians in live use|Stakeholder buy-in achieved via promotional video
featured.learned.heading: What I Learned as a PM
featured.learned.body: The biggest challenge was not building the system: it was designing it for people with deeply ingrained workflows. I learned that adoption is a product problem, not a training problem. If users need a manual to use it, the design failed. I also learned that a promo video is a legitimate PM deliverable: getting stakeholders aligned on value before they see the product is part of the job.
contact.closing: I'm actively looking for junior Product Manager roles where I can contribute from day one. If my background looks like a fit, or if you're just curious, I'd love to connect.

featured.decisions.cell2.title: Structure data at source
